subject: Residency & regional cost — $/1M token target and budget bands
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Prieto <sam.prieto@finservpro.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: residency tradeoffs + $/1M token target (recap & asks)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Sam — quick recap and focused asks so we can build a scoped pilot that fits your procurement window. Key points from our side and the items we need to lock down: 

- Volume profile you shared: ~3–5M tokens/month in Q2, stepping to 15–25M tokens/month by Q4 (mix of chat + assistant completions).
- Residency requirement: customer data (user prompts + outputs) to remain in EU for EU users; US residency for US users. You indicated mixing is acceptable so long as EU stays in-region.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target around $750–$1,200 per 1M tokens (all-in) depending on SLAs, model family, and residency premium.

As discussed, two levers materially move cost: (1) model family/size (LlamaX-13B vs LlamaX-70B variants), and (2) residency premium (~15–30% delta we see on our side depending on cloud egress and compliance controls).

Requests / next steps: 
1) Can you confirm an internal target $/1M token for procurement (pick a single number or a tight band) so we can price to that anchor?
2) Please confirm the expected % of EU-located traffic vs US for token volume by user cohort (rough split or a small sample of traffic patterns).
3) Procurement timeline and required contracting items (Sow/SLA/PO cadence) — is a 60-day procurement window realistic for your team?

I've attached the token model workbook and a one-page residency cost breakdown that shows our estimated delta between US-hosted vs EU-hosted serving for the same model profile. Marissa will pull together a pilot quote once we get your anchor $/1M and the traffic split.

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: finservpro_token_model_v2.xlsx (token mix & calc), residency_cost_breakdown.pdf (US vs EU delta)

From: Sam Prieto <sam.prieto@finservpro.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@finchain.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency tradeoffs + $/1M token target (recap & asks)

Thanks Vivek — useful summary. A couple clarifications from our procurement side: 

- For Q2 we should be conservative: 3M tokens/month (mostly US users), by Q4 we expect the EU user base to ramp faster than we initially modeled — call it 40% EU / 60% US at peak.
- On the $/1M target: procurement wants an anchor at $900/1M tokens for budgeting purposes. They understand that EU residency could add premium; if you can show a clear break (e.g., base $900 -> EU-hosted $1,080 = 20% uplift), that helps our finance ask.
- SLA expectations: standard enterprise 99.9% uptime for user-facing endpoints; lower-cost batch/rerank endpoints can be 99.5%. We might want flexible fallbacks (US-hosted lower-cost model) for non-sensitive workloads.

Procurement timeline: 45–75 days depending on legal redlines. PO likely in April if we can get a straight pilot price and an MSA track.

Cc'ing Olivia who will coordinate technical proof-of-concept details.

—Sam
Director, Product Integrations
FinServPro

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Prieto <sam.prieto@finservpro.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency tradeoffs + $/1M token target (recap & asks)

Perfect — thanks for the anchor, Sam. Action plan from Redwood: 

1) Marissa will produce a 60-day pilot quote scoped to: 3M tokens/month baseline, US-hosted baseline at $900/1M, EU-residency uplift at 20% (so $1,080/1M for EU-hosted traffic). Quote will show blended price for a mixed traffic split and an explicit line-item for residency premium so procurement can see the math. (Target: draft quote in 3 business days.)
2) Ben will draft an SOW template that includes data residency controls, KMS integrations, and the fallback routing policy for non-sensitive workloads.
3) Technical POC: Olivia to share sample traffic profile and a small prompt set; Marissa will propose a minimal test matrix (latency targets, model variant, and token caps).

If the 20% delta looks off to you after you review the residency_cost_breakdown.pdf, flag it and we can iterate — the workbook has knobs for different cloud regions and storage/access patterns.

I'll set a 1:1 with procurement owners if needed. Marissa — can you confirm you'll have the draft pilot quote by end of Friday (Mar 5)?

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: finservpro_token_model_v2.xlsx, residency_cost_breakdown.pdf
